note: A1+ Unit 2 Lesson 2.5, built on 2026-11-19 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. The user approved the A1+ Unit 2 plan on 2026-11-19 (A1+ 2.Y follows A1 2.Y, one grammar step each) and chose "Straight to Preview": no per-lesson gates, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, reviewed in Preview. Revised the same day after the user's Preview test ("the person is just looking at this one but person does not point at the other bag or item for that one"): each scene now has a THIS photo and a THAT photo from the same camera behind the speaker (Ana's red and blue bags, Luis's white and black bikes, Diego's green and black chairs; the bag and bike scenes also with the colors swapped). In THIS the speaker looks down at the near thing and touches it; in THAT the speaker faces the far thing, only the back of the head shows, and the arm points down at it (user choices: "maybe they need to be two image transitions?", "turn him more", "dont show his eyes", "lower his hand"). A but sentence plays as two turns by the same speaker, THIS photo then THAT photo, so the picture switches on but; its own picture (picture cards, Use) is the THAT photo, which shows both things. The cups became bikes because a far cup is too small on a phone. The pointing line spans the 3:2 frame, so no 2.5 photo goes into a four-picture card. Only the person in the photo says this and that. Use builds the two halves and, because the whole but sentence is 9 words and Use takes at most 8, the short form with 2.4's isn't (This one is red, but that one isn't.).

lesson.title: 2.5 This one, but that one
lesson.unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
lesson.unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
lesson.goal: Contrast a near thing and a far one with but (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.) and say this one and that one instead of repeating the thing (This one is red, but that one is blue.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.5 This and That: A1 says This is a phone. for a near thing and That is a phone. for a far one; A1+ 2.5 sets the two against each other in one sentence. The one new grammar relationship is but joining two taught clauses (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.), with this one and that one standing for the thing (A1 2.10's Which one? The red one.): This one is red, but that one is blue. Each scene has two photos from the same camera behind the speaker: in the first the speaker looks down at the near thing and touches it (this), in the second the speaker faces the far thing and points down at it (that). A but sentence plays as two turns, so the picture switches on but. Two scenes are also photographed with the colors swapped, so a picture card tells this from that, not the color alone.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 2.5 this and that; A1 2.8 colors; A1 2.10 Which one? The red one.; A1 3.12 This car is mine. (this + noun); A1 2.3 bag, chair; A1 2.2 bike; A1+ 1.5 Do you have…?
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say but short and weak (/bət/) with a small pause before it; stress the two colors (This one is RED, but that one is BLUE). Say this with a short i and that with an open a. Do not require native-like speed.
